articles.title: "Hard to fall asleep": Spurs' Victor Wembanyama unveils lasting effects of NBA Finals to Knicks
articles.summary: Victor Wembanyama and the Spurs had a lot to say after processing their loss to the Knicks at NBA Media Day.
articles.body:
Coming so close to the Larry O'Brien Trophy but losing has major effects on a team. The San Antonio Spurs had all offseason to process the grief of losing to the New York Knicks . On NBA Media Day, they let their emotions out and revealed how they dealt with such a tough experience. Victor Wembanyama may have had one of the worst things happen to him, which could prompt an even bigger burden to prove himself for the 2026-27 season.

Victor Wembanyama reveals he and Spurs lost sleep after NBA Finals defeat to Knicks

The Spurs have all that it takes to get back up on their feet to once again become NBA title contenders. Coach Mitch Johnson has the luxury of a young core that features Victor Wembanyama, Dylan Harper , Devin Vassell , and Stephon Castle . Adding in a veteran like Tobias Harris means that they will likely be more stable for the 2026-27 NBA season. A lot of their championship hopes have to start somewhere. For the Spurs, it all revolved around getting over the grief of losing to the Knicks in five games.

Wembanyama seems to be the most affected among all of the Spurs players. Some go to the practice facilities and forget the loss ever happened. This is not the case for the Spurs superstar. In fact, he felt one adverse effect that may have increased the size of the chip on his shoulder. He saw the grief manifest through disruptions in his circadian rhythm, via Jared Weiss of The Athletic.

"It's been hard to fall asleep sometimes. Hard emotions. But there is a point where you accept that you have to go through it. You have to feel it all. We don't want to hide from anything," Wembanyama declared on Spurs Media Day.

Everything was going the Spurs' way during the 2025-26 NBA season. They jumped up to 62 wins and got the second seed in the Western Conference. Their hardest matchup was the 64-win Oklahoma City Thunder led by Shai Gilgeous-Alexander . By the Western Conference Finals, any worry about Coach Johnson's schemes and choices was thrown out the window. It was because they beat the best team in the NBA in a seven-game series. Then, all hell broke loose.

The Knicks battered them in Game 1 with a 10-point margin (105-95). A lot of hope was in the air for Game 2, but the Spurs still fell short by two points to get the win (105-104). For a moment, Wembanyama and Co. thought the tide was shifting because they won Game 3 (115-11). However, all of those specks of hope withered away in a painful manner. The immaculate tip-in by OG Anunoby had them lose Game 5 (107-106) to go down 3-1. The hole the Spurs were in had grown too deep by then. It all culminated in a 94-90 Game 5 loss as the Spurs saw another team hoist the Larry O'Brien trophy.

The Spurs vow not to let that happen to them again, to themselves and to their fans. If all goes well, it seems like Wembanyama will secure a second NBA DPOY, his first NBA MVP, and NBA Finals MVP. All of that would put him alongside David Robinson and Tim Duncan in the upper echelon of Spurs bigs to have won the Larry O'Brien trophy.

Losing sleep is one thing, but Wembanyama knows better. He will start and end the season in ways that will turn the tide towards the Spurs. For someone who sleeps very early, he surely will not want his circadian rhythm interrupted again.

articles.title: Los Angeles Lakers' Biggest Questions at Training Camp
articles.summary: Luka Dončić is the clear leader of the Los Angeles Lakers as the franchise heads into its first season in the post-LeBron James era.
articles.body:
Luka Dončić is the clear leader of the Los Angeles Lakers as the franchise heads into its first season in the post-LeBron James era.

The trio of Austin Reaves, Walker Kessler and Dončić will compete in a loaded Western Conference with high expectations and hopes for a deep postseason run.

Can L.A. compete with the likes of the San Antonio Spurs and Oklahoma City Thunder? Will the squad defend well enough to thrive in the postseason? Who will round out the starting five?

The Lakers enter the 2026-27 campaign with questions that can only be answered over time, setting up what should be a watchable, unpredictable season.

Late last week, coach JJ Redick was clear on three of the team's starters with Dončić, Reaves and Kessler, while the remaining two would be decided throughout training camp.

Tongue-in-cheek, Redick noted the pair rounding out the starters "will not be two white guys."

Regardless of the remark, the reality is the Lakers do not have two clear next-best players. Redick's lack of obvious choices reflects the roster's top-heavy construction.

That doesn't mean others will emerge as the perfect fits. Quentin Grimes, 6'5", is listed by the NBA as a guard, but he's the initial favorite to be the fourth starter. That's a tall three-guard lineup with Kessler (7'2"), Dončić (6'8"), and Reaves (6'5"). Grimes would take on tougher defensive assignments, tertiary playmaking, and complementary scoring/shooting.

That leaves the question mark at power forward. Candidates include Sandro Mamukelashvili, Ziaire Williams, Adou Thiero, Jake LaRavia, Jarred Vanderbilt, Kevon Looney and Matisse Thybulle. Each has different strengths and weaknesses.

Mamukelashvili, one of the Lakers' top offseason acquisitions, adds offense, but not defense. Vanderbilt, LaRavia, Looney and Thybulle are more productive defensively, but less so on the other end of the floor, and some have durability issues.

A tremendous camp from either Williams or Thiero could be the answer for Redick.

The Lakers have 16 guaranteed standard contracts on the roster and need to get down to 15 by opening night. The franchise projects to be over the luxury tax by almost $500,000 and $8.1 million below its first-apron hard cap. Waiving a player like Dalton Knecht would solve the roster dilemma.

But if getting under the tax is a priority, the Lakers could trade that extra player, like Knecht, for cash and/or a second-round pick. With no player coming back, that would give the Lakers a $4.2 million trade exception and time to evaluate the roster before making a more significant move.

Top basketball executive Rob Pelinka recently said the team can consider a 2-for-1 trade. While he didn't name candidates, the standard-contract players Pelinka and Redick didn't mention in last week's press conference were Jaden Hardy, Vanderbilt, LaRavia and Knecht. That could have been an oversight, or it may indicate their importance to the Lakers' primary decision-makers.

Los Angeles has one clean first-round pick swap and three second-rounders to offer as incentives if a starting-caliber power forward becomes available in the next few weeks. More likely, the Lakers will wait to see what they have for a more dramatic move, but the NBA has seen more late-summer trades over the past few weeks than usual.

While Kessler missed most of last year with a shoulder injury, he was one of the league's best rim-protecting centers during the 2024-25 season with the Utah Jazz. At the same time, the Jazz were among the league's worst defensive teams.

The point is, the Lakers won't magically become a dominant defensive squad by plugging Kessler in at center. The perimeter defenders have to do their job as well. Redick expressed confidence that his team already has what it needs to do so, but press conferences are not under oath and involve a certain level of salesmanship.

For example, at a similar pre-training-camp press conference two years ago, Redick sidestepped a question about whether the team needed a traditional center. L.A. acquired Deandre Ayton the following summer and added Kessler this past July.

The Lakers' defensive potential looks iffy, which may not be a major issue in the regular season but could be a bigger liability in the playoffs. Still, the front office may wait until trade season (December 15 through the February trade deadline) to address proven needs, rather than act on a preconceived notion of what they lack.

Should Mamukelashvili win the starting spot at power forward, the only center coming off the bench would be Looney, who is listed by the NBA as a 6'9" forward.

In his best years with the Golden State Warriors, Looney averaged below 24 minutes per game. If Kessler needs to sit out for an extended period, Looney is ill-equipped to start.

Mamukelashvili is a talented offensive player, but he's not considered a strong rim protector. He may not start, serving as Kessler's primary backup with Redick going with offense in reserve. Looney is a smart, experienced player and a viable option when the Lakers need an undersized, switchable defender.

Ultimately, L.A. is one center short and needs someone who can play a role similar to Kessler's as a rim protector, screen setter and lob threat.

The Lakers' top-three players should fit well together. Dončić and Reaves bring substantial offensive firepower. Kessler fills a vital need at center. Then, Collin Sexton, Grimes and Mamukelashvili round out the team's primary attackers offensively.

The team has a lengthy list of role players who could contribute, including Bronny James, Ziaire Williams, Matisse Thybulle, Adou Thiero, Cameron Carr and Kevon Looney. Redick faces a difficult task in establishing a viable rotation.

Still, the Lakers are top-heavy. Like all NBA teams, health is vital. L.A. has a thinner margin than other franchises with deeper rosters. Catching the Spurs and Thunder in the standings doesn't seem realistic. The Lakers are in that next group, fighting off the Denver Nuggets, Houston Rockets, Golden State Warriors, Minnesota Timberwolves, Portland Trail Blazers, and any other Western Conference squads that coalesce.

As constructed, the Lakers should be a fun watch, winning close to 50 games, but their postseason viability is questionable unless the defense is significantly better than projected.

Discounting Dončić, one of the league's most talented offensive players, would be a mistake. In the first year without LeBron James, the Lakers are still reconfiguring around their star.

The front office may need at least one more trade deadline and another offseason to push into elite status, but Victor Wembanyama and the Spurs could remain a major obstacle for the foreseeable future.

Email Eric Pincus at eric.pincus@gmail.com and follow him on X/Twitter @EricPincus .

articles.title: El Kosner Baskonia refuerza su pintura con Marcio Santos
articles.standfirst: El pívot brasileño de 2,04 metros y 23 años jugó la temporada pasada en el Maccabi Tel Aviv
articles.summary: El pívot brasileño de 2,04 metros y 23 años jugó la temporada pasada en el Maccabi Tel Aviv
articles.body: El Kosner Baskonia ha incorporado al brasileño Marcio Santos a su juego interior con un contrato por dos temporadas, según anunció este martes. El jugador de 2,04 metros es natural de Brasil, tiene 23 años, y procede del Maccabi de Tel-Aviv, donde promedió 6,9 puntos y 2 rebotes por duelo. El nuevo baskonista, que ocupará plaza de extracomunitario junto a Markus Howard y Kenneth Faried, comenzó su carrera y se desarrolló como jugador en el equipo brasileño Franca desde la campaña 2018-2019 hasta la 2024-2025. Posteriormente, debutó en Europa con el Ratiopharm Ulm en la BBL para pasar después a las filas del Maccabi. El interior brasileño también cuenta con experiencia como internacional con la selección absoluta de Brasil. El club baskonista indicó en una nota de prensa que suma a "un jugador físico, con energía y con experiencia en Europa".

articles.title: The NBA's next first-time All-Stars? Best bets, players knocking on the door and long shots
articles.summary: Six players made the All-Star Game for the first time in 2026. Here are my top 24 choices this season, ranked by tiers.
articles.body:
Six players made the All-Star Game for the first time in 2026: Deni Avdija , Jalen Duren , Chet Holmgren , Jalen Johnson , Jamal Murray and Norm Powell. Who could make their first All-Star appearances in 2027? Here are my top 24 choices, ranked by tiers:

2025-26 Stats: 21.0 PPG | 6.7 RPG | 4.5 APG | 51-Point Game at 19

The Case: Flagg averaged 25.2 points, 7.2 boards, and 5.3 assists over his final 26 full games last season. He was already one of the game's 15 to 20 best players for a stretch of his rookie year. With Kyrie Irving back , his efficiency should improve even more. And even putting aside Kyrie, Flagg could take a leap in Year 2 of his career regardless.

The Hurdle: If Irving's return isn't what the Mavericks are expecting and the team struggles again, the team might not win enough games for voters to give Flagg the nod over players on winning teams. All-Stars will inevitably be in Flagg's future, it's just a matter of when.

2025-26 Stats: 16.2 PPG | 5.8 RPG | 2.7 APG | 38.9% 3PT

The Case: Gordon was averaging 20.3 points while shooting 45.2% from 3 and playing his typically excellent defense to begin last season, all before a hamstring injury derailed his year. But the way the year started hasn't left my mind. Gordon was doing all his typical off-ball scoring alongside Nikola Jokić , but also doing more off the dribble in the post, out of isolation, and in pick-and-rolls. If that type of production carries over to this season, and if he stays healthy, the Nuggets could have first-time All-Stars in consecutive years.

The Hurdle: Will Gordon stay healthy for the first time in a few years? And will he get enough scoring opportunities? The Nuggets might be at their best with Gordon sharing the floor with Jokić, but that doesn't mean he'll put up the raw numbers to be named an All-Star.

2025-26 Stats: 23.3 PPG | 4.7 RPG | 5.5 APG | 64.1% TS

The Case: Reaves was averaging 28.9 points through his first 18 games last season, so we've already seen him look like an All-Star. But then he got injured and that derailed his bid for a spot. If he and Luka both stay healthy this season, this could be the year. Reaves averaged 19.6 points per 75 possessions on 62.5% true shooting alongside Luka, and an astounding 33.1 points on 65.9% true shooting without him, per DataBallr. So he can thrive next to Luka and take over when Luka sits.⁣

The Hurdle: Reaves competes on defense, but opponents can still target him. He might end up the weak link that teams attack this season. Becoming more reliable at the other end would make it easier to argue that the Lakers deserve multiple All-Stars.

2025-26 Stats: 18.3 PPG | 7.8 RPG | 5.3 APG | 3.0 OREB

The Case: Thompson earned my Defensive Player of the Year vote in 2024-25, and I voted him onto my All-Defensive second team last season. So he's already established as one of the game's best defenders, and last season he became an 18 point per game guy. Given the way Amen impacts the game across the board, it'd be surprising if he wasn't named an All-Star at some point in his career. Maybe this is the year it happens. And even though Fred VanVleet will cut into his playmaking chances, maybe he'll end up scoring more as a shooter, cutter, and rebounder.

The Hurdle: Thompson's improvement to 77.9% at the free throw line offers some hope for his jumper, but he still made only 21.6% of his 3s last season. Defenses will keep backing off until he gives them a reason to stop. And without the jumper it could be quite hard for him to put up enough points.

2025-26 Stats: 20.6 PPG | 5.2 RPG | 3.3 APG | 34 Games Played

The Case: Wagner made 82.3% of his free throws and 51.6% of his floaters last season. Those numbers have been consistently great going back to college. But his 3-pointer has never clicked. Could this be the year? If so, expect his scoring averages to jump big time. He already has every other skill: He scores inside, he's a talented passer, he does the dirty work, he rebounds and he's a great defender. What more could you want? Well, a jump shot.

The Hurdle: We're entering Year 6 of his career, and we're still having the same conversation about his jumper. Maybe it's just never going to happen.

2025-26 Stats: 17.4 PPG | 3.4 RPG | 4.0 APG | 36.2% 3PT

The Case: White will have space to get downhill into the paint and he's a potent shooter beyond the arc. We didn't see a lot of White without LaMelo Ball on the floor last season, but in the 282 minutes that we did he averaged 33.2 points and 7.2 assists per 75 possessions. The Hornets have enough faith in their existing roster to live without LaMelo, and White could prove to be worth the bet.

The Hurdle: White was more of a 20-points-per-game guy in Chicago prior to this surge with Charlotte. So we may have already seen his peak level. Last season's surge could have just been more about the fact defenses weren't game planning for a backup guard the way they did for LaMelo.

2025-26 Stats: 20.8 PPG | 3.4 RPG | 3.7 APG | 39.9% 3PT

The Case: Alexander-Walker jumped from 9.4 to 20.8 points per game last season. What if there's more coming? His elite shooting already makes defenders sweat, he's a talented connective passer, and a versatile defender. Better finishing and self-creation could vault him higher. He led Team Canada in pick-and-rolls this summer, ahead of Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Andrew Nembhard . So perhaps that usage is a sign of what's to come.

The Hurdle: Alexander-Walker's breakout was built largely on off-ball volume. He ranked in the 30th percentile in isolation scoring and the 37th percentile in pick-and-roll scoring, per Synergy. So as optimistic as one might be, these numbers would have to improve a lot for him to fuel the scoring jump needed to earn a spot.

2025-26 Stats: 16.7 PPG | 5.3 RPG | 7.4 APG | 1 40-Point Triple-Double

The Case: Castle checks a lot of boxes already as an elite defender who can bully his way into the paint, and catch fire as a scorer. If he becomes a more reliable pull-up shooter, then he has All-NBAs, not just All-Stars, in his future.

The Hurdle: Castle has never really been a consistent shooter going back to high school, so it might be wishful thinking for it to suddenly come along. And with De'Aaron Fox and Dylan Harper sharing the backcourt, Castle might end up more of the third wheel.

2025-26 Stats: 23.6 PPG | 3.7 RPG | 6.1 APG | 37.1% 3PT

The Case: George averaged 23.6 points on 60.9% true shooting last season, which are borderline All-Star numbers as is. With a stronger roster around him now, George could see an uptick in assist opportunities this year as the primary ball-handler on the team. With continued improvement as a scorer on his drives to the rim and more playmaking chances, an All-Star appearance is a realistic goal.⁣

The Hurdle: George has been a poor defender so far in his career. Without some progress on that end, it could hurt the Jazz and his chances of getting this honor.⁣

2025-26 Stats: 17.0 PPG | 8.3 RPG | 9.1 APG | 13 Triple Doubles

The Case: Giddey is already flirting with triple-double averages. More stops on defense could lead to a couple more rebounds, and more made shots could lead to a couple more assists. The Bulls being better could really be all it'll take for Giddey to become a 20/10/10 guy.

The Hurdle: The Bulls drafted Caleb Wilson, who looked like a blossoming star in Las Vegas Summer League. What if Wilson is so good that he's taking touches away from Giddey? Maybe Giddey's numbers could even drop. Or conversely, the Bulls might continue to be a bad or mid team, and a great stat line for Giddey won't be enough for voters to reward him.

2025-26 Stats: 20.2 PPG | 4.9 RPG | 3.3 APG | 38.3% 3PT

The Case: Miller scored 26.7 points per 75 possessions, compared with 23.5 alongside LaMelo last season, per DataBallr. Now without LaMelo on the squad, those numbers could become more of a regular occurrence. But he can't just be an empty calories numbers guy. Miller's efficiency needs to approach or exceed 60% true shooting and he needs to maintain competitive defense.⁣

The Hurdle: It was another offseason spent rehabbing. Miller had surgery on his left shoulder in May, so a summer that could have been devoted to expanding his game became another recovery period. Maybe this will turn out to be a good thing and he'll finally be healthy, though.

2025-26 Stats: 21.5 PPG | 5.7 RPG | 3.8 APG | 12 3s in One Game

The Case: Murphy has steadily added to his game since entering the league. He's such a dangerous shooter, and he's developed the ability to beat some defenders off the dribble. Murphy's offseason training focuses on these creation moments, so if he starts building on it then his already impressive numbers could balloon.

The Hurdle: The Pelicans. I don't expect New Orleans to be a playoff team, and the West is loaded with stars on teams that will be. Murphy could have the best season of his career and still lose out to someone putting up similar numbers for a contender.

2025-26 Stats: 16.7 PPG | 5.2 RPG | 2.2 APG | 1 Finals Game-Winner

The Case: We just watched Anunoby score 20 points per game during a championship run. Why can't some version of that carry over if the Knicks continue to spread the ball around? His defense has long been worthy of All-Star consideration. More scoring could finally get him there.

⁣ The Hurdle: OG took only 11.6 shots per game during New York's title run. The reason he scored so much is just that his efficiency was outrageous. But his volume wasn't all that different. During the regular season, he's never averaged more than 18 points or attempted 14 shots per game. There might simply be too few shots available for OG to put up the numbers voters need to see.

2025-26 Stats: 20.1 PPG | 4.1 RPG | 4.1 APG | 39.1% 3PT

The Case: Bane's usage was at 23.3% last season. Could new Magic head coach Sean Sweeney simply put the ball in Bane's hands more often? Bane averaged 23.7 points per game in Memphis on a 28.5% usage before, so even though he's a shooter first he's not just a specialist. Bane is a good pick-and-roll shot creator and could handle a heavier workload.

The Hurdle: There's a lot of mouths to feed in Orlando. Paolo Banchero and Franz Wagner need the ball too.

2025-26 Stats (5 games): 14.4 PPG | 10.8 RPG | 3.0 APG | 1.8 BPG

The Case: When Kessler is defending the basket, opponents shoot only 50.6% on shots within six feet of the rim. That is 13.3% worse than their average in those situations, a purely dominant mark that now will be in the Los Angeles limelight. On offense, Luka Dončić is about to make his life easy by spoonfeeding him shots at the rim. Kessler also began shooting 3s last season, so if that carries over then he could put up bigger numbers than anyone is really anticipating.⁣

The Hurdle: Rudy Gobert is a three-time All-Star but a four-time Defensive Player of the Year and a nine-time All-Defensive player. The point is that dominant defenders aren't always honored for their efforts. Kessler will need to have a career-best year on offense, and with a ton of talent on that end for the Lakers he might just end up being a guy cleaning up inside.

2025-26 Stats: 24.2 PPG | 7.1 RPG | 3.0 APG | 3.4 3PM

The Case: Before the All-Star break last season, MPJ averaged 25 points, 7.2 rebounds, and 3.2 assists. I thought he belonged on the All-Star team, despite how horrible the Nets were. But he didn't get the nod from coaches in part because Brooklyn was such an eyesore. Maybe this year the Nets will be better, and maybe Porter will put up comparable stats that get more love.

The Hurdle: Julius Randle will command some of the touches that belonged to Porter, who had a lot of freedom last year. So Porter needs to show that his first half was a level he can sustain while sharing more of the offense.

2025-26 Stats: 17.0 PPG | 3.9 RPG | 5.2 APG | 37.7% 3PT

The Case: Without Jaylen Brown on the floor last season, Pritchard averaged 26.7 points and 7.6 assists per 75 possessions on 60.6% true shooting. This year, Pritchard could end up the No. 2 scorer in Boston so there could be a lot more chances coming for him to bomb 3s, get into the paint, and run the offense.

The Hurdle: It's unclear whether Pritchard will start or how much more of the offense he'll control. Just because Brown is gone, it doesn't mean he'll suddenly become a featured guy. Jayson Tatum will get more touches, too, and so will Paul George and others on the roster.

2025-26 Stats: 14.1 PPG | 10.6 RPG | 2.2 APG | 3.4 OREB

The Case: If Tyrese Haliburton returns looking like himself, Zubac will feast off his playmaking. We could even see them become the league's most potent pick-and-roll duo. But Zubac is also a great post scorer and an excellent interior defender. All those pieces together could make him one of the keys to Indiana's turnaround and earn him an All-Star spot.

The Hurdle: Even if Zubac is great, he needs enough touches in an offense with Haliburton, Pascal Siakam , and lots of other shot creators on the team.

2025-26 Stats: 12.1 PPG | 11.6 RPG | 2.1 APG | 1.7 BPG

The Case: Clingan shot 34.1% from 3 on 3.2 attempts per game while anchoring Portland's interior defense. Last season, opponents shot 12% worse than they ordinarily did on shots within six feet when Clingan was the closest defender. So, he could be blossoming into one of those rare bigs that can both space the floor and put a lid on the rim.

The Hurdle: An All-Star case will require sustaining his production beyond last season's 27.2 minutes per game.

2025-26 Stats: 11.8 PPG | 3.4 RPG | 3.9 APG | 18.0 Finals PPG

The Case: Harper shot 25.2% from 3 and 57.3% at the rim before the All-Star break, then 47.9% and 66.7% afterward, respectively. Then he averaged 18 points in the Finals. Those season-long averages listed above undersell just how excellent he was to finish his rookie year. With another year of seasoning, he could explode.

The Hurdle: There are a lot of mouths to feed in San Antonio: Castle, De'Aaron Fox, and, of course, the big tall French guy. Harper could be better, but it doesn't mean he'll get enough touches or play enough minutes.

2025-26 Stats: 18.5 PPG | 5.3 RPG | 3.4 APG | 273 3s (Rookie Record)

The Case: Knueppel is already one of the NBA's best shooters, but he ranked only 15th with 7.9 3-point attempts per game. Could he see that number climb to nine or even 10 without LaMelo Ball absorbing so many touches anymore? Perhaps. But spot-up shooters don't make All-Star games. And Knueppel's ability to handle the ball and make smart passes is what sets him apart from those specialists. Kon ranked in the 76th percentile for pick-and-roll scoring efficiency last season, and there will be a lot more chances to show what he can do with the ball in his hands.

The Hurdle: A left hamstring injury will cost Knueppel the preseason, and he won't be reevaluated until the first week of the regular season. So he's already starting behind, so much so that I considered removing him from the list. But he still deserves a mention when this list is 24 names long.

2025-26 Stats: 14.8 PPG | 4.2 RPG | 2.7 APG | 41.2% 3PT

The Case: McDaniels already has established himself as one of the game's greatest defenders. With Julius Randle and Naz Reid gone, the Wolves could need him to take on more on-ball scoring responsibility and LaMelo Ball could help by finding him on cuts, in transition, and for open 3s. If more buckets go his way, then so too could an All-Star appearance.

The Hurdle: Anthony Edwards and Ball will control much of the offense and take most of the shots. So even an uptick in scoring for McDaniels might not be enough to make it.

2025-26 Stats: 9.9 PPG | 5.7 RPG | 3.1 APG | 1 Steals TItle

The Case: Ausar is already one of the best defenders in basketball, but he played only 26 minutes per game last season. Maybe now he'll eclipse 30 minutes. Thompson can do everything on offense except shoot, but he also works his butt off to develop that skill. Maybe this is the year it clicks.

The Hurdle: Ausar took only 24 3s last season, and he made just six of them. It'd be quite a monumental leap if he starts becoming a reliable guy from outside.

2025-26 Stats: 16.5 PPG | 4.4 RPG | 5.4 APG | 1.3 BPG

The Case: What if White just remembers how to shoot? He made 32.7% of his 3s last season after shooting 38.1%, 39.6%, and 38.4% in his previous three full seasons with Boston. White is already an elite defender and connective passer. So without Jaylen Brown, and more opportunities potentially available, he simply needs to get back to shooting the way he has before to have a chance to have his best season.

The Hurdle: White was a streaky shooter prior to that hot three-year stretch in Boston. What if he just goes back to the way he was before? White can still help Boston win games, but he'll have to score to be named an All-Star.

articles.title: NBA Drops Video Announcing New 'Points of Emphasis' for Referees During 2026-27 Season
articles.summary: The NBA underlined the new Points of Emphasis for their referees heading into the 2026-27 season.
articles.body:
The NBA underlined the new Points of Emphasis for their referees heading into the 2026-27 season.

One such focus is offensive players using their off-arm to push off and create space from a defender. The league also wants officials to make sure screeners are being properly penalized when they do more than just get in the defender's way:

The Points of Emphasis didn't neglect guidance for defensive players. The NBA wants players off the ball to have the necessary space to move around the perimeter and into the paint. Contact on straight-line pathway plays should warrant a foul as well.

This is about enforcing rules already in the book rather than introducing new ones. Still, there's always a bit of an adjustment for players early into the season as they discover what they can and can't get away with.

Don't be surprised if there are more whistles than usual in the first few weeks as the league attempts to set a baseline.

articles.title: NBA Training Camp Rumors Live Blog
articles.summary: Media days are in the rearview and training camps are underway all over the NBA.
articles.body:
The Oklahoma City Thunder unloading Luguentz Dort, Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins had to be motivated, at least in part, by the fact that the younger players on the roster are about to get a lot more expensive.

And the first name on that docket might be guard and defensive ace Cason Wallace, who's averaged 8.5 points, 2.6 assists and 1.9 steals in 27.0 minutes over his last two seasons.

For OKC, paying anywhere near his max (over $200 million for five years) would be ludicrous, but they might not be able to afford to lowball him either.

Wallace could become a full-time starter with Dort gone, and his production will likely go up as a result. If he has a big 2026-27 without that extension in place, keeping him in restricted free agency in 2027 will be tougher.

Given what he's done so far, something around $100 million for four years may seem steep, but it could also age into a bargain.

articles.title: Reporters caught on hot mic gossiping about how annoying but attractive Ben Simmons and Zach LaVine are
articles.summary: A livestream captured a hot mic moment as reporters called Ben Simmons and Zach LaVine "hella fine" during Sacramento Kings NBA media day.
articles.body: The Sacramento Kings hosted an official media day on Monday and the big takeaways for at least a few reporters in attendance were that Ben Simmons and Zach LaVine are both "cringe" individuals, but also "hella fine." A number of local affiliates livestreamed the Kings' media availability on Monday, but it was NBC's KCRA that captured a hot-mic moment that has taken over social media. Instead of the live stream being cut, or at the very least muted between players talking to reporters, KCRA's rolled on, and two female reporters in attendance were caught making quite the admissions about LaVine and Simmons. SOCIAL MEDIA ERUPTS OVER NEW BROADCASTING GUIDELINES THAT DISCOURAGE 'SEXUALIZED' SHOTS OF FEMALE ATHLETES As one of the reporters explained that she was working on transcribing Simmons' earlier interview, she was heard saying he was "cringe cringe," before another woman responded, "you lucky you so fine." "He’s a good-looking dude," the first reporter said before the second agreed by stating, "hella fine." "I didn’t notice, his skin is like so smooth," the first reporter continued. "I was like, ‘damn, no tattoos?" The attention later turned from Simmons to LaVine when a male reporter asked, "What about Zach LaVine?" to which one of the females responded, saying he was "hella fine" as well. The other female reporter made it clear that she wasn't a fan of LaVine's persona. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! "I think his personality annoys the sh-t out of me," she said. "Zach’s cute but his personality f–king annoys me. It just seems he’s like he’s hella like a prick." SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER LaVine is entering what will be his third season in Sacramento after leading the Kings in scoring a year ago, averaging 19.2 points per game, but he managed to appear in only 39 games after suffering a hand injury that required season-ending surgery in February. As for Simmons, he signed a one-year deal with the Kings in early September after going unsigned for the entirety of the 2025-26 NBA season. He last played in an NBA game in April 2025 with the Los Angeles Clippers.

articles.title: 76ers, Cavs, Penguins, More Unveil New Concession Menu Items for 2026 NBA, NHL Seasons in Photos
articles.summary: With the 2026-27 NHL season getting underway and the NBA season on deck, Aramark unveiled some new concession offerings at arenas around the country.
articles.body:
With the 2026-27 NHL season getting underway and the NBA season on deck, Aramark unveiled some new concession offerings at arenas around the country.

No NBA team is generating more excitement than the Philadelphia 76ers after they added Jaylen Brown and LeBron James in the offseason. At home games for the Sixers and Philadelphia Flyers inside Xfinity Mobile Arena, fans can expect culinary specialties like red chile short rib tacos, a short rib corn dog, chicken Milanese and a chicken gyro.

Rocket Arena, home of the Cleveland Cavaliers, is introducing Delia's, a new stand on the main concourse that specializes in fried chicken.

Pittsburgh Penguins fans will be able to partake in some beef birria tacos and Tex-Mex chicken quesadillas at the new Insta Grill! at PPG Paints Arena. The tacos include Jalisco-style braised beef and Oaxaca cheese. The quesadillas treat eaters to Cajun-seasoned chicken, roasted corn, black beans, cheddar jack and a roasted red pepper crema.

As they attempt to defend their Western Conference crown, the San Antonio Spurs are bringing back their Culinary Residency Program to Frost Bank Center. Spechts Texas, Nanay's Bakery, Wok Wey and Magnolia Pancake Haus are some of the restaurants taking part.

The premium hospitality spaces at Canadian Tire Centre, Brookstreet Lounge and Club Bell, in Ottawa were renovated to give select Ottawa Senators fans an even more luxurious experience.

The Sen-Sational Poutine Burger is the concessions headliner. The burger is made of Canadian bison and includes poutine gravy, cheese curds and smashed potato tots.

articles.title: Lakers' JJ Redick Recalls Quentin Grimes Mistakenly Entering Neighbor's Hamptons House in 2023
articles.summary: Before Los Angeles Lakers head coach JJ Redick had veteran guard Quentin Grimes on his roster, he tried to do him a solid earlier in his career.
articles.body:
Before Los Angeles Lakers head coach JJ Redick had veteran guard Quentin Grimes on his roster, he tried to do him a solid earlier in his career.

During Monday's media day, Redick recalled a hilarious story from the summer of 2023 when he invited Grimes to his Long Island home to stay at his guest house for a workout. Grimes, who was entering his third season with the New York Knicks at the time, arrived to the house along with his friend while Redick was out playing golf.

"So I give him the [address], and I tell him where the key is to get in," Redick told Spectrum SportsNet (5:10 mark). "I said, 'When you walk in, there's a first-floor bedroom. There's a second-floor bedroom. Make yourself at home. There's a gym down in the basement. Everything you need.' Very clear."

However, when Redick got back to his place, he didn't find Grimes in his guest house.

"I go on his Instagram, and he's posted a picture from another house in my neighborhood of the pool, with the hashtag 'Hamptons Life' or something like that. So I tell him, 'Where the F are you, dude?'" Redick recalled. "They had gone into one of my neighbors' homes and gone into their guest house."

Despite the early faux pas, Grimes still made a strong impression on Redick and his family during their brief time together.

"We took him out to dinner that night with my kids and my wife, and we had a nice time," Redick said. "Then we were going to the gym the next morning, and we were traveling separately, so my wife called me at eight o'clock in the morning. She says, 'How do we ensure that our kids grow up to be like Quentin?' and that's a strong stamp of approval from Chelsea Redick."

Grimes is one of the many new faces that the Lakers will be integrating this season, but it sounds like Redick is already confident in his chances to fit right in as the team chases a spot in the playoffs.

articles.title: Una hora con el genio: “Si vas a apostar, apuestas por mí, no contra mí…”
articles.standfirst: MARCA, testigo directo de una conversación excepcional con Michael Jordan sobre la evolución del deporte, la tecnología, los negocios y su pasión por competir
articles.summary: MARCA, testigo directo de una conversación excepcional con Michael Jordan sobre la evolución del deporte, la tecnología, los negocios y su pasión por competir
articles.body: Michael Jordan ya no juega, pero sigue compitiendo. Lo hace desde los despachos, desde la propiedad de equipos, desde las inversiones y también desde un deporte tan diferente al baloncesto como la NASCAR. En Lisboa, durante una hora, dejó algunas de las claves de cómo entiende el deporte de hoy: los datos, la tecnología, los aficionados, las marcas, la expansión global y, por encima de todo, la necesidad de seguir siendo fiel al deporte. A sus 63 años, el seis veces campeón de la NBA continúa vinculado al deporte desde distintos frentes y su presencia pública sigue siendo poco habitual. Por eso una hora con Jordan tiene algo de acontecimiento. Y MARCA tuvo la oportunidad de vivirla en el Super Stage del MEO Arena, dentro del SBC Summit Lisboa 2026. El escenario reunió a Jordan con Carsten Koerl, fundador y CEO de Sportradar, y Jason Robins, cofundador y CEO de DraftKings, en una conversación bajo el título 'Leadership in Sports Business'. El encuentro abordó la evolución del deporte, la tecnología, los datos, los medios, la relación con los aficionados y la transformación del negocio deportivo. Pero, en realidad, todo acababa conduciendo a una misma pregunta: ¿qué queda de Michael Jordan cuando desaparece la cancha? La respuesta, que apareció varias veces durante la conversación, es simple: queda la competición. “Nunca me preocuparon las estadísticas”, así arrancó la leyenda del deporte. Jordan escuchó hablar durante buena parte de la charla de datos, inteligencia artificial, mercados de predicción, seguimiento de jugadores, nuevas experiencias para los aficionados y de un deporte cada vez más medido. Y entonces recordó cómo veía él el juego. “Como jugador, nunca me concentré realmente en eso”, explicó. “Estaba ahí jugando a mi deporte. Y el único objetivo que tenía era ganar el partido”. Una frase sencilla, pero que probablemente explique mejor que ninguna otra cómo entiende Jordan la transformación del deporte. El baloncesto que él dominó era otro. No existía la cantidad de información disponible hoy, ni el seguimiento constante de cada movimiento, ni la posibilidad de que un aficionado pudiera estar pendiente en tiempo real de prácticamente cualquier estadística de un jugador. Hoy todo está medido. Jordan, sin embargo, sigue pensando como entonces. “No puedo preocuparme por lo que la gente está apostando. No puedo preocuparme por las estadísticas. Lo único que me importa es el final del partido”. Es, probablemente, una de las grandes diferencias entre el deporte de su época y el actual. El aficionado ya no solo observa. Participa, apuesta y sigue estadísticas a un ritmo frenético. Construye su propia narrativa y sigue a jugadores y no únicamente a equipos. Pero para Jordan hay una frontera que no debería desaparecer: la del deportista concentrado en competir. Ese cambio fue uno de los grandes temas de la conversación. Jason Robins explicó cómo las apuestas y el fantasy han creado nuevas formas de conexión con el deporte. Carsten Koerl llevó la conversación todavía más lejos: los datos han dejado de ser una infraestructura invisible para convertirse en parte del propio espectáculo. Y Jordan también lo ve. “Los aficionados de hoy tienen una mejor comprensión o están mucho más centrados en el resultado. Y están dispuestos a involucrarse en ese resultado”. Durante la charla le plantearon una cuestión inevitable: ¿cómo habría vivido Michael Jordan el baloncesto actual? La respuesta fue inmediata. “Si jugara hoy, ¿cómo sería el juego? Es un deporte completamente diferente”. Pero su conclusión no cambió. “Simplemente jugaría, nunca me habría preocupado de quién estaba apostando por los Bulls, quién no estaba apostando por los Bulls, cuál era el spread (hándicap de puntos de las apuestas deportivas)”. Porque, para él, existe una responsabilidad que sigue siendo individual. “Como atleta solo puedo influir en una cosa: lo que hago en la cancha de baloncesto. Fuera de eso, no tenemos el control”. Y ahí apareció otro de los grandes cambios del deporte moderno. Antes, explicó, el jugador podía salir a la cancha y jugar. Hoy tiene que construir una marca, cuidar sus números, pensar en sus contratos, gestionar su imagen y atender a todo un ecosistema que existe alrededor de su rendimiento. “Hoy tienes que construir una marca”, dijo. “Tienes que preocuparte por cuáles son tus números en términos de la recompensa económica que vas a recibir al final de tu contrato”. Jordan entiende perfectamente ese nuevo escenario, pero no parece sentir nostalgia por él. “Me alegro de haber nacido en la época en la que nací”. Y terminó soltado una broma... que sonó más a una verdad absoluta. Ahora, los apostadores buscan centrarse en las debilidades de los jugadores para ver en qué apostar, algo que no cree que pueda aplicarse en su caso. "No soy un buen ejemplo para vosotros. Soy el peor contra el que apostar. Si vas a apostar, apuestas por mí, no contra mí", sentenció. Si hay un lugar donde se entiende mejor al Jordan posterior al baloncesto es NASCAR. No porque sea un territorio natural para una leyenda de la NBA, sino precisamente porque demuestra que su manera de entender los negocios no depende del deporte. “A todos nos gusta conducir rápido. Algunos reciben multas. Otros no. Pero nos gusta conducir rápido”. Jordan lo dijo entre risas al explicar su relación con NASCAR, pero detrás de la frase hay mucho más. La leyenda del baloncesto creció rodeado de carreras. Su padre era un apasionado de los coches y la familia acudía a circuitos como Darlington, Charlotte o Rockingham. Esa relación terminó desembocando en 23XI Racing, la escudería que fundó junto a Denny Hamlin en 2020. En 2026, 23XI ha seguido dando motivos para hablar. Tyler Reddick ganó las primeras dos carreras de la temporada, incluida la Daytona 500, y Jordan no ha ocultado la emoción que le produce ver a su equipo competir por las victorias. Pero la aventura no se limita a competir. “Si puedo generar un impacto o cambiar algo, entonces merece la pena el desafío”, explicó durante la charla. “Las cosas en las que me involucro son muy auténticas respecto a quién soy”. No quiere decir que invierta únicamente en aquello que conoce. Quiere decir que existe una conexión entre su imagen, sus intereses y aquello que representa. “Cuando me involucro en negocios, ya sea DraftKings o Sportradar, es auténtico respecto a lo que me representa y a cómo conecto con esa persona o con esa empresa”. Jordan sabe perfectamente que su presencia tiene un valor añadido. “Sabiendo que, por mi posición, voy a ser un vehículo de marketing para ello, el consumidor tiene que conectar con eso”.

articles.title: Anadolu Efes - Real Madrid en directo | Última hora de Euroliga en vivo hoy
articles.summary: El conjunto madridista ya está calentando sobre el parquet. No hay billetes en Estambul para recibir al Real Madrid. El Turkcell Basketbol Geliim Merk
articles.body:
Última hora del Anadolu Efes - Real Madrid

¡¡¡Muuuy buenas tardes y bienvenidos a todos y todas a la segunda jornada de la Euroliga !!! El Real Madrid afronta su segunda salida de la temporada para visitar a un viejo conocido. Los de Pedro Martínez se enfrentan al Anadolu Efes de Pablo Laso , con el objetivo de conseguir su primera victoria .

El conjunto blanco debutó en la Euroliga con derrota por la mínima (78-77) en la cancha de Dubai , en un partido errático y con un marcador bajo, alejado de los parámetros del exentrenador de Valencia Basket y de lo ofrecido en la Supercopa Euroliga que consiguieron llevarse.

Hace apenas dos días, el Real Madrid consiguió vencer a Unicaja en el debut de Liga Endesa ante Unicaja en otro partido apretado, y para este encuentro frente a los turcos , Pedro Martínez podría contar con Nick Smith Jr ., el escolta anotador que ha llegado desde la NBA .

Delante, el proyecto de Anadolu Efes liderado por Pablo Laso . Esta temporada, con tiempo para trabajar desde el inicio del curso, y con una plantilla más potente que la anterior, con piezas importantes como Mike James, Dario Saric o Matthew Strazel , a la que también se ha incorporado el español Santi Yusta . Efes cayó derrotado en el Palau Blaugrana el jueves pasado ante el Barcelona (89-82).

Desde las 19.00 horas , el Real Madrid visita Estambul para buscar su primera victoria europea y aquí estaremos para vivirlo con todos vosotros y contarlo, como siempre, en MARCA .

articles.title: Shaquille O'Neal se moja: "El juego europeo es un poco mejor que el de la NBA"
articles.standfirst: El legendario pívot, de visita en Kaunas, ensalzó el baloncesto europeo en detrimento del estadounidense antes de presenciar el Zalgiris-Olympiacos de Euroliga
articles.summary: El legendario pívot, de visita en Kaunas, ensalzó el baloncesto europeo en detrimento del estadounidense antes de presenciar el Zalgiris-Olympiacos de Euroliga
articles.body: Shaquille O’Neal ha llegado a Kaunas dispuesto a vivir en primera persona la pasión de la Euroliga y se ha marchado de Vilnius dejando una frase que va a levantar polvareda al otro lado del Atlántico. “Sé que el juego europeo es un poco mejor que el juego de la NBA. Sé que me van a criticar mucho por decir eso”, aseguró el cuatro veces campeón de la NBA antes de acudir al Žalgirio Arena para presenciar el duelo entre el Zalgiris y el Olympiacos, vigente campeón de Europa. El exjugador de Lakers, Magic, Heat, Suns y Celtics explicó los motivos de su inesperada preferencia. “En la Euroliga se juega un baloncesto duro los 38 partidos. En la NBA hay un poco de relajación hasta el All Star o los playoffs”, afirmó. Shaq, que sólo ha presenciado un partido de baloncesto europeo en directo, espera comprobar esta noche en Kaunas la intensidad que tanto le han contado: “Fue una locura. Estoy deseando ver cómo de intenso y loco será este partido”. Pero O’Neal fue todavía más allá al explicar qué diferencia, a su juicio, a ambos mundos. “Siempre he dicho que los europeos tienen fundamentos de baloncesto mucho más fuertes que los jugadores estadounidenses”, señaló. Su diagnóstico también incluyó una comparación de estilos: “Los americanos pueden tener más talento y saltar más alto, pero los europeos primero juegan al baloncesto con la cabeza, mientras nosotros nos gusta utilizar nuestras capacidades atléticas”. La visita a Lituania también le permitió reivindicar a algunos de los grandes interiores europeos que dejaron huella en la NBA. Shaq recordó especialmente a Arvydas Sabonis, con quien protagonizó duelos memorables, y quiso reencontrarse con él en su país: “Espero darle un abrazo cuando le vea... Esto será cuestión de respeto y amor. Cuando ocurra, le diré: ‘Gracias’”. También elogió a Jonas Valanciunas, del que destacó sus 14 años en la NBA y su capacidad para utilizar el cuerpo y la fuerza cerca del aro. Y dejó una última receta para conquistar Europa que resume bastante bien su visión del baloncesto: “Necesitas uno o dos grandes jugadores y construir el equipo alrededor de ellos. Especialistas defensivos, tiradores y, sobre todo, quererlo más que nadie”. Shaq ha llegado a Kaunas como embajador de NordVPN, pero su visita al Zalgirio Arena ha acabado convirtiéndose en algo más: una reivindicación pública del baloncesto europeo frente a la NBA desde la voz de una de las mayores leyendas de la historia de la liga estadounidense.

articles.title: A'ja Wilson and Breanna Stewart put Las Vegas Aces and New York Liberty on brink of series sweeps
articles.summary: A'ja Wilson's 38-point, 16-rebound Game 1 masterclass left the Indiana Fever reeling as the Las Vegas Aces eye a WNBA Playoffs series sweep.
articles.body: The WNBA Playoffs are upon us, and all eight teams played on Sunday. Instead of sending all of them back tonight, we have two games and four teams taking the court. I am going to share a play in both games. I know that the WNBA has a lot wrong with it, but I feel like the opening round being just a best-of-three is a bit rough (I feel the same about the MLB). Playoffs should be at least five games, and with these matchups, I want as many as I can get. Aces vs. Fever The Las Vegas Aces are defending champions and still turned in one of the better regular seasons this year. They have the best player on the planet, A'ja Wilson. They hosted the Fever in Game 1 and beat them by 17 points. It was an ugly game for Indiana, but it was a very impressive performance from Las Vegas. The Fever had no answer for Wilson, who poured in 38 points and hauled in 16 rebounds. She did it on an incredibly efficient 15-for-19 shooting as well. WNBA PLAYOFFS PREVIEW: WHY THE FEVER AT +145 COULD BE THE BEST BET AGAINST DEFENDING CHAMPION ACES The starting lineup for the Fever just couldn't get much going. Caitlin Clark had 15 points, but wasn't overly efficient from the field, and she didn't even get to the free-throw line. She chipped in 10 assists, but also had six turnovers. Single-season scoring leader Kelsey Mitchell had 12 points, but she was just 4-for-16 from the field. If the Fever want to stay alive, they need to double Wilson and make someone else beat them, and they need to be much more efficient on offense. I think the right play here is to take the Aces at -102 on the moneyline. I just don't think the Fever have enough answers for the Aces, even though I picked them to win the series. Getting a road victory is definitely a requirement for anyone who is an underdog in a series. The New York Liberty are the 8th seed, but as I mentioned in my preview of the series, the Liberty were picked preseason as the favorite to win the WNBA Championship. Now they are one game away from ending the season of the best team in the league (at least via regular-season record). Game 1 went to the Liberty, even though they won the game on the road. It wasn't just a win; it was kind of a blowout, with the Lynx losing by 16. Breanna Stewart showed why she is one of the best in basketball and poured in 34 points. The Lynx didn't get much from their two best players, Napheesa Collier and Olivia Miles. They combined for just 23 points and 9-for-26 shooting. With their backs against the wall, I think the Lynx will get the win, but I do think it could be a very close game. The Lynx are 18-4 on the road this season so winning on the road shouldn't be new to them. I expect defense to be key for Minnesota tonight. Give me the under 173.5. articles.title: Former Knicks and Cavs standout J.R. Smith arrested in Texas on assault charge
articles.summary: J.R. Smith spent 16 seasons in the NBA, winning two championships.
articles.body:
Former New York Knicks and Cleveland Cavaliers standout J.R. Smith was arrested in Texas on an assault charge Monday, per jail records . TMZ was first to report Smith's arrest.

Smith — whose given first name is Earl — was arrested by the Royse City Police Department on a charge of assault. The official jail record mentions both "bodily harm" and "family violence" in the description of the charge on Smith's record.

No additional details were given regarding Smith's arrest and no bond has been set for the former 16-year NBA veteran.

Smith, a former first-round pick by the New Orleans Hornets , developed into an off-the-bench star after being traded to the Denver Nuggets . He spent five seasons with the team, often contending for the Sixth Man of the Year award.

After a brief stint in China, Smith returned and signed a deal with the Knicks, where he eventually won the Sixth Man of the Year award. During the 2014-15 NBA season, Smith was traded to the Cavaliers to try and help LeBron James win a championship. The Cavaliers succeeded the following year, giving Smith his first NBA championship.

Years later, Smith reunited with James on the Los Angeles Lakers . Smith played in just six regular-season games with the team before seeing time in 10 playoff games with the franchise and winning another title.

Following that victory, Smith decided to enroll back in college and take up golf. He graduated from North Carolina A&T State University in May 2026.

Smith previously served 24 days in jail in 2009 after pleading guilty to reckless driving stemming from a 2007 crash that resulted in one death.
